sentiment.instructions: Judge the sentiment the tweet's author conveys, either their own feeling or the clearly good or bad nature of what they report. Topic words (dates, names, 'may', ordinals) do not count, and neither do exclamation marks or 'lol' on their own. When there is no clear positive or negative leaning, choose neutral.

criteria.positive: Explicit positive feeling: excitement ('can't wait', 'fast forward to', 'celebrate', 'perfect night', 'for sure going'), love, praise, pride, gratitude, hope, or warm wishes and prayers. Also the author inviting people to join their own event or outing ('come with us', 'come support', 'let's go'), or happily indulging in a favorite thing. Also reports of completed good outcomes: a win, title, record, history made, someone delighted. Also promotions pushing appealing tickets, prizes or free items ('get your tickets now', 'win', 'don't miss').
criteria.neutral: Bare plans and logistics with no stated enthusiasm. Also plain event listings, routine group meetings or hangouts, info sessions and sign-ups. Also questions, requests, fan pleas, trivia, jokes, memes, spam and incoherent text. Also in-progress game updates, speculative headlines ('may'), mild comparisons of politicians or players, and wire-style celebrity news. Also comic jabs at public figures, teams or companies ('Bwahaha', 'clear as mud', 'didn't get the memo'). Also minor hiccups reported with a workaround or apology. Also fandom melodrama or mock gripes ('lol', 'lmao', 'I'm dead', 'not ready', 'v sad', 'Nooo').
criteria.negative: Earnest frustration, anger, disappointment, sadness, fear, insult or criticism ('sucks', 'disappointed', 'hate', 'shameful', 'NOOO' at news, 'miss'). Short grumbles or digs also count ('don't know why they haven't...', mocking a day or a person, 'no talent'), as do pointed arguments or accusing rhetorical questions against someone's view. Also reports of harmful events: attacks, missiles, deaths and funerals, crimes and arrests, crashes, deficits, devices breaking, conflict.
